Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re finalizing requirements for Arkadia’s production rollout (targeting GA in Q1) and procurement asked for a clear set of dedicated reservation options tied to expected traffic and SLAs. High level:

- Expected steady-state: ~200 inference req/s across a mix of short (2-4k tokens) and long (30k token) requests, ~60% chat-like requests with KV cache reuse.
- Peak bursts: up to 450 req/s for short windows (10–20 min).
- Latency SLO: P95 < 220ms for short requests, P95 < 800ms for long-context workflows.
- Compliance: Must run in a dedicated private cluster (VPC) with KMS and audit logs.

Can you send 2–3 reservation profiles with: recommended min GPUs for the cluster, suggested ramp schedule (weeks to prime KV caches), an approach for burst capacity (reserved vs. burst credits), and an initial cost direction we can share with finance? Also include a canary rollout suggestion. Procurement included in cc (procurement@arkadia.ai).

I attached the RFP excerpt that calls out compliance and retention needs.

Appreciate a crisp options matrix we can circulate to procurement by Friday.

- Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP. I pulled together three high-level reservation profiles (attached) for procurement that map to different risk/cost tradeoffs. Quick summary here so you can share with finance:

Option A — Conservative Reserved (Lower latency risk)
- Minimum reservation: 96 A100s equivalent (shared across two AZs)
- Ramp: 10 weeks (20% increments every 2 weeks), full pre-warm before week 10
- Burst: Dedicated burst pool (20% buffer) + cross-region failover
- Notes: Best P95 outcomes for long-context; higher upfront commit.

Option B — Balanced (recommended for expected profile)
- Minimum reservation: 64 A100s equivalent
- Ramp: 8 weeks (25% increments every 2 weeks), auto-prefix cache seeding during ramp
- Burst: Burst credits + short-term on-demand spill to a compatible quantized variant
- Notes: 10–15% lower unit cost than pure on-demand, preserves cost flexibility.

Option C — Flexible/Cost-saver
- Minimum reservation: 40 A100s equivalent
- Ramp: 6 weeks, aggressive autoscale policy (slower scale for long-context jobs)
- Burst: Heavier reliance on on-demand + model variant fallbacks for long tails
- Notes: Lowest commit; larger risk to P95 for long-context workloads.

I attached redwood-reservation-options.xlsx with assumptions (token mix, concurrency, estimated token/sec), and a one-page canary plan. Karthik added some technical constraints and pre-warm notes — tagging him to expand on GPU sizing for long-context jobs.

Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk through numbers.

Adding technical commentary to Connor's options — Elena, copying Connor and Marissa so procurement sees the tradeoffs: 

- GPU sizing for long-context: long-context work (20–30k tokens) consumes KV cache and memory bandwidth. Practical sizing shows ~1.8x token-cost per request vs short requests. For 250 req/s mixed profile, Option B (64 GPUs) maps to ~55 sustained long-context concurrent sessions before P95 degrades; Option A (96 GPUs) gives headroom (~85 concurrent long-context).

- Minimum reservation floor: For guaranteed P95 targets, we recommend a hard floor per AZ of 16 GPUs to avoid single-AZ saturation during maintenance — i.e., Option B -> 64 GPUs across 2 AZs = 32 GPUs/AZ.

- Ramp & pre-warm: KV-cache priming can be done in parallel with canary traffic. Recommend a 2-phase pre-warm: (1) synthetic cache seeding during week 1–3, (2) gradual live traffic seeding during week 4–8. This reduces long-tail latency during cutover.

- Autoscale mechanics: For long-context scaling we suggest conservative scale-up thresholds (longer windows) to avoid thrashing; short requests can scale faster. This affects how much burst you need as reserved vs. on-demand.

- Procurement/finance note: reserving extra burst pool (20%) vs relying on on-demand has different unit economics vs. SLA risk. I added a simple TCO table in the workbook (see tab "TCO_by_option").

If helpful, I can produce a mapping matrix that converts Arkadia’s traffic levels (+0%, +25%, +50%) to recommended reservation sizes and expected P95 ranges.

—Karthik

Subject: Final recommendation: Minimum SLA reservation strategy for Arkadia (Option B, recommended)

Elena / Raj / procurement team — thanks for the quick responses. Based on Arkadia's growth profile, long-context sensitivity, and procurement's ask for a clear cost/commitment tradeoff, our recommended path is Option B (Balanced). Highlights and next steps below: 

Recommendation summary (Option B)
- Reserve: 64 A100-equivalent GPUs across 2 AZs (32 GPUs/AZ) as the committed floor.
- Canary: Isolated canary slice leveraging the same cluster but traffic-tagged; begin with 5% traffic (week 1), ramp to 20% by week 3, full cutover after week 6 subject to success criteria.
- Ramp schedule: 8 weeks total. Suggested cadence: 25% capacity increments every 2 weeks (16 GPUs increments). Pre-warm plan: week 1–3 synthetic seeding + week 4–8 live seeding.
- Burst strategy: Maintain 20% reserved burst buffer plus short on-demand spill to compatible quantized variants for sudden spikes. Cross-region failover configured for critical endpoints.
- SLA mapping: P95 targets — short requests < 220ms (expected actual ~180–200ms); long-context P95 < 800ms (expected ~600–700ms with Option B and recommended pre-warm).
- Minimum operational constraints: 32 GPUs/AZ to allow rolling maintenance without impact; isolate control-plane endpoints to the private VPC.

Cost & procurement notes
- Estimated incremental committed cost: see attached workbook tab "TCO_by_option". Option B reduces unit token cost ~12% vs on-demand while retaining flexibility. Exact numbers in the workbook are modeled for +0%, +25%, +50% traffic scenarios.

Action items
1) Procurement: confirm procurement contact for contract/docusign (cc’d procurement@arkadia.ai).
2) Technical: confirm whether you want a dedicated isolated canary cluster (adds ~8 GPUs to initial reservation) or the tagged-slice approach above.
3) Sign-off: once procurement confirms, we’ll issue a formal reservation proposal/quote (includes SLA annex and SOC2 evidence pack).
